title: Regular quotients from parameter approximations in all finite jets
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$, and put $d=\dim_\kappa(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)$. Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal and fix an integer $0\leq s\leq d$. Suppose that for every integer $n\geq1$ there are elements $u_{n,1},\ldots,u_{n,d}\in\mathfrak m$ whose classes form a $\kappa$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and such that $$J+\mathfrak m^{n+1}=(u_{n,1},\ldots,u_{n,s})+\mathfrak m^{n+1}.$$ Then $A/J$ with its induced local structure is a regular local ring of Krull dimension $d-s$. The elements may depend on $n$; no compatibility between these tuples is required. The ideal generated by an empty tuple is zero.

source.place: Lemma 13.3, printed p.255, together with 13.2, printed p.254: lifts of a cotangent basis form a regular system of parameters; the approximation criterion permits the system to depend on n.

proof.text: Put $B=A/J$ and $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak m/J$. The quotient-local and Noetherian-image lemmas make $B$ nonzero Noetherian local, with residue field $\kappa$. The graded criterion applied to the regular ring $A$ gives $\dim A=d$. For each $n\geq1$ put $I_n=(u_{n,1},\ldots,u_{n,s})$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian. Nakayama applied to this $A$-module and its quotient $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ shows that the full $d$-tuple generates $\mathfrak m$. The parameter-quotient lemma therefore makes $C_n=A/I_n$ regular local of dimension $d-s$.

source.place: Lemma 13.3, printed p.255, proof; 13.2(a),(b), printed p.254.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq1$. Since $\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subseteq\mathfrak m^2$, adding $\mathfrak m^2$ to the assumed equality gives $J+\mathfrak m^2=I_n+\mathfrak m^2$. For $q=1$ and $q=n$, set
$$T_q=(\mathfrak m^q+J)/(\mathfrak m^{q+1}+J)=(\mathfrak m^q+I_n)/(\mathfrak m^{q+1}+I_n).$$
For $q=n$, both numerator and denominator agree: add $\mathfrak m^n$ to the assumed equality for the numerators. The map $a\mapsto a\bmod J$ identifies the first expression with $\mathfrak b^q/\mathfrak b^{q+1}$: it is surjective and its kernel on $\mathfrak m^q$ is $\mathfrak m^q\cap(J+\mathfrak m^{q+1})$. The same formula with $I_n$ identifies the second with the degree-$q$ piece for $C_n$. Both residue-field identifications are the identity on $\kappa$.

source.place: Lemma 13.3, printed p.255, proof; 13.2(a),(b), printed p.254.

proof.text: Under these identifications the maps $\mu_{B,n}$ and $\mu_{C_n,n}$ of the graded criterion are the same map $\operatorname{Sym}^n_\kappa(T_1)\to T_n$: on a product of classes represented by $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathfrak m$, both send it to the class of $a_1\cdots a_n$. Such products span the symmetric power by its definition in the criterion; the degree-one identification induces the symmetric-power identification by sending each product to the product of its images, with inverse induced by the inverse identification. Since $C_n$ is regular, the criterion makes this map an isomorphism. Thus $\mu_{B,n}$ is an isomorphism for every $n\geq1$, and the reverse direction of the criterion makes $B$ regular local. Finally, at $n=1$, $T_1=(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2)/\langle\bar u_{1,1},\ldots,\bar u_{1,s}\rangle$, which has basis the remaining $d-s$ classes. Hence the dimension clause of the criterion gives $\dim B=d-s$. Only one tuple is used for each degree; the empty tuple and empty remaining basis give the same argument for $s=0$ and $s=d$.

The item is Lemma 13.3, stated with d = dim m/m^2 and cotangent-basis lifts that may change with n; step 1 links these to Milne's regular system of parameters through Nakayama. The statement is unchanged, and its citer lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth step 6 meets its hypotheses. Step 1: the cited statements of quotient-local-structure, surjective-image-noetherian, the new criterion's dimension clause (dim A = d), Nakayama's iff form on M = m, and the c = s clause of regular-local-generators-regular-sequence each say what the step takes, so C_n = A/I_n is regular of dimension d-s. Step 2 is genuinely elementary: J+m^{q} = I_n+m^{q} for q = 1, 2, n, n+1, and b^q/b^{q+1} = (m^q+J)/(m^{q+1}+J) with the kernel as stated. Step 3 compares the canonical maps on spanning products, not some abstract isomorphism. It uses the forward direction for C_n and the converse for B, one tuple per degree, and gets dim B = d-s from T_1. Edge cases checked: s = 0, s = d, d = 0. The hypothesis correctly fails for J = (y^2) in k[x,y]_(x,y). New node lem-sfb-regular-local-graded-cotangent-criterion: B is regular iff Sym^q(n/n^2) -> n^q/n^{q+1} is an isomorphism for all q >= 1, and then dim = e. It is true (Milne 13.2(a), Matsumura 14.4, Stacks 00NO; the converse goes through Hilbert-Samuel 00KQ). Small cases checked: a field, k[t]/(t^2), k[x,y]/(xy). It is statement-only and self-contained, and every notion cites a node. It is not a clause of the item.
